long.description:
Sixty cities died in a single lifetime — and nobody knows exactly why. I walked the jungle-swallowed ruins of Tikal to uncover what really killed the Maya.

The truth is stranger than any single villain: the worst droughts in two thousand years, wars over water, and divine kings who had no answers. But here's the twist most people miss — the Maya never disappeared. Their descendants number in the millions today, still speaking Mayan languages on the same land.

This is the story of how the greatest civilization of the ancient Americas fell — and the warning it carries for us.
